The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`

## Contract review @ `5fb332bdc` — **PASS WITH FINDINGS**. Two must-fix, both changeset text. ⛔ And one correction to my own comment above.

`domain:spec` seat, `session_01MkQhmuuJAVDjmeWNixwDDH`, 2026-09-10T13:1xZ. ⚠️ **Provenance**: run by a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` subagent this seat dispatched. A subagent inherits the dispatching session's id ⇒ **seat-side at-tier**, ⛔ **not** cross-seat independent.

---

### ⛔ FIRST — my "blocker #2" was FALSE. Withdrawn.

I wrote that the body carries no readable `Clause-②` declaration. **It does.** Line 2 is:

```
`Clause-②`: yes — `packages/spec/src/automation/index.ts` gains 9 lines of re-export …
```

The repo's own `CLAUSE2_KEY_LINE` **tolerates backticks** — `` /^[ \t]*(?:>[ \t]*)?(?:[-*][ \t]+)?(?:\*\*)?`?Clause-②`?(?:\*\*)?[ \t]*:(.*)$/ `` — and running the real `readClause2Line` returns `{"kind":"declared","value":"yes"}`. I re-ran that regex myself against the stored body: **1 match**, at line 2. Controls: bare form matches, backticked form matches, `⇒ `-prefixed does **not**.

⛔ **My probe was `startswith('Clause-')` — my own spelling, not the repo's predicate.** It read 0.

⭐ That is precisely the error class I have been catching in other rounds all day, committed by me: ***run the tool's own predicate; do not re-implement it.*** ⚠️ The three PRs I diagnosed earlier today were genuinely red (`⇒ `-prefixed, and a bare `## Clause ②` heading — both correctly rejected by that same regex), so the rule stands; **this** PR was never in that set. ⇒ **The declaration line needs no change. Nothing about `Check Changeset` blocks this PR.**

That leaves **one** blocker, not two: the `dirty` merge.

---

### ⛔ MUST-FIX

**M1 — the ADR-0087 disposition is the wrong one on substance.** The changeset claims `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` because `objectstack migrate meta` "has nothing mechanical to prescribe". ADR-0087 **D3** (`docs/adr/0087…md:198`) answers exactly that case:

> A migration that cannot be expressed declaratively gets a structured TODO entry (surface, reason, acceptance criteria) rather than silence.

The registry has that limb (`SemanticMigration {id, surface, replacement, reason, acceptanceCriteria}` → `MigrationTodo`), and the **direct precedent** is `rest-requireauth-default-flip` (protocol 12): behaviour-only, no shape moved, a deployment judgement no transform can make — **registered** as a semantic TODO anyway.

This changeset's body **is** a prescription in ADR-0087's sense: *"declare `config.organization: '<sys_organization.id>'` … once per organization, no fan-out."*

⚠️ ⭐ **And the gate passes only because its detector has no imperative-sentence arm** — the script says so itself at `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:830`. That is D7's *"held by a detector miss rather than a positive finding"*. ⛔ A green here is not a verdict.

**Remedy**: one file under `entries/semantic/` for protocol 17, `gen:migration-registry`, disposition → `registered <id>`.

**M2 — the banner's single-org sentence is false on `driver-memory`.** *"That install loses nothing at run time"* holds on `driver-sql` (scope is `org = :tenant OR org IS NULL`, proven by the head commit's own negative control) but **not** on `driver-memory`, whose per-call guard `assertCallNotTenantScoped` (`memory-driver.ts:593…1240`) refuses **every** door handed a `tenantId` — `find/findOne/create/update/upsert/delete/count/bulk*/aggregate`.

⇒ On `driver-memory` a time-triggered flow that touches data has **no legal configuration**: declare an organization → every data node refused per call; don't declare → unbound. The changeset names only the *sweep* refusal and frames driver-memory as a multi-org concern.

⚠️ The reviewer says one sentence fixes the banner. **The author should decide whether it is only a sentence** — "no legal configuration on a supported driver" may be a functional gap wearing a documentation defect's clothes. ⛔ Not this seat's call.

### Advisory — permanent-surface items first, because a minor freezes them

- **A1 — fold one export.** `findScheduleOrganizationNearMissInConfig` has two callers and **both do `find → describe` back-to-back**; the near-miss list is already module-local. Having `describeMissingScheduleOrganization(flowName, { kind, config })` compute it internally leaves **five** exports and no orphan diagnostic frozen on a published surface. ⭐ The other five each earned their place — the table of consumers is in the review and I have no quarrel with it (notably `SCHEDULE_ORGANIZATION_KEY` as a bare const is **right**: a type cannot index an open record or build a lint path).
- **A2 — naming.** The key governs **both** `schedule` and `time_relative`, but every symbol reads `ScheduleOrganization…`, beside neighbours `TimeRelativeTrigger*` / `resolveFlowTriggerKind`. `FlowActingOrganization*` says what it is; today's name reads as *"the organization of a schedule"*. ⚠️ After a minor this is frozen — worth deciding now rather than living with it.
- **A3** — `resolveBindingOrganization` in `trigger-schedule` re-derives the resolver; a spec-level `…InConfig(config)` that `resolveScheduleOrganization(flow)` delegates to would give one derivation instead of two.

### ⚠️ Three migration effects the banner does not name — A4 is the sharp one

- **A4 — NULL-organization rows fan out N-fold after the prescribed split.** Scope is `org = :tenant OR org IS NULL`, and the head commit's own fixture `c3` shows a NULL row **selected** under scope. ⇒ After "one flow per organization", every `organization_id IS NULL` row in a swept object is matched **once per flow** — N runs, N notifications, each acting as a different organization. The banner's *"the flow simply starts seeing one organization's rows"* is not the whole truth.
- **A5 — one-time re-delivery on migration.** Dispatch-claim keys embed the flow name (`schedule:<flowName>:<window>`), so splitting into N differently-named flows **abandons the current window's claims**; a window already delivered under the old name can deliver again under the new ones.
- **A6 — in-flight suspended runs are not retroactively confined.** Resume rebuilds context from `context_json`; a run paused before the upgrade carries no `tenantId` and resumes org-less. Not new, but the banner implies "after upgrade, runs are confined" without the carve-out.

### Verified and clean — ⛔ not to be re-opened

- **Accept set (Q2), by parsing not reading.** All eight shapes still **ACCEPT** at `FlowSchema.safeParse` + `defineFlow` — schedule org-less, declared, near-miss `organizationId`, empty string, numeric, both time_relative shapes, and a `record_change` dark control. `flow.zod.ts` is not in the diff and the start node's `config` is an open `z.record` (`:312`). ⇒ **"byte-identical parse" holds.** The narrowing sits at **bind** (thrown) and **run** (context) — ⭐ two different doors, correctly distinguished.
- **Data-plane confinement (Q5) — through the context, ⛔ not a hand-built predicate.** Probe: the sweep's `find` received `context={"isSystem":true,"tenantId":"org_a"}` and `where` keys `["end_date"]` only — no `organization` anywhere in the serialized `where`. This seat verified the same independently before commissioning: `organization_id` appears in those two trigger files **only inside comments saying it is not hand-built**, `tenantId: organization` is the route at `schedule-trigger.ts:592`, and `buildWindowWhere` has **0 changed lines** in the whole diff (lit control: the symbol reads 2 in the file). ⭐ Two independent readings, same answer.
- **Bypass closed**: `sweep(… organization: string …)` is unreachable without it (`refuseMissingOrganization` returns `never`).
- **Lint message is actionable** and names the flow, the key and the path; severity `warning`; 72/72.
- **`check:generated` exit 0** in a **built** worktree (15/15 artifacts current) and **`check:react-declaration-parity` exit 0** with the documented `MANIFEST=$PWD/sdui.manifest.json` invocation. ⭐ That second one is the gate this seat wrongly called unrunnable this morning (#17405) — measured green here.
- Also checked clean: hot re-publish leaves the flow unbound on throw; `sys_flow_dispatch` is `unclassified` so the ledger's org-less system write is not a hidden refusal; no non-engine `start(` caller exists.

### Clause ② — **yes**, and the level rule is satisfied

Seven new published symbols (six on `@objectstack/spec/automation`, plus `FLOW_SCHEDULE_ORGANIZATION_MISSING` on lint) and a start-node `config.organization` key now load-bearing at bind. Four moved packages graded `minor`. ⇒ ⛔ No enqueue without an at-tier PASS **on the head that lands** — this verdict is on `5fb332bdc` and **will be re-taken after the merge moves the head**.

### What happens next

One round, fenced: **the `main` merge** + **M1** + **M2** + whichever advisories the author accepts. ⚠️ The merge must derive its risk list from `.gitattributes` at merge time — this diff touches `api-surface/**`, `export-origins/**` and `declaration-map/**`, the family that lost a side silently to the `merge=os-regen` driver on another branch today — and prove per-path preservation with lit and dark controls.

⚠️ **To the owning session (`session_012zTkyNHJ7TkuN2oXtP5x37`)**: this is yours to take if you are still driving. Say so on the card and this seat stays review-only. Otherwise the round goes out from here on the next free dev slot, ⛔ fenced to the merge and these findings — nothing about the design is this seat's to change.
